operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: election=5 rows, representative=7 rows; original_values lists are complete, no rowid sampling needed.
All columns notnull=0 and null_rate=0.0; no NULLs in original, but schema permits them.
election.Representative_ID FK -> representative.Representative_ID; parent PK unique, all 5 child values (1,2,4,5,7) exist in parent (7 rows).
election.Date is TEXT storing mixed formats: 'July 1942', 'October 1942' (month-name), and bare years '1946','1949','1953'.
representative.Lifespan is TEXT with en-dash U+2013 ranges: '1947–', '1868–1930', '1923–', '1916–2003' — not a parseable date.
All numeric columns declared INT/REAL but stored as integer/real storage classes; Votes/Seats/Place are whole-valued reals (9423.0, 6.0).
Vote_Percent distinct=4 of 5 rows (tie present); Seats distinct=4, Place distinct=3 — duplicates exist in original.
Party has only 2 distinct values (Republican/Democratic); State 5 distinct; Name 7 distinct (all unique).
No composite keys, no self-references, no dangling FKs, no unique/check constraints beyond PKs.
Table/column names are mixed-case with underscores ('Election_ID','Vote_Percent'); must be double-quoted.
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent table `representative` in FK clause — sqlite_master DDL replay must preserve it.
election.Date declared TEXT dispatches to String fuzzer, not Date — text-stored dates will get random strings.
operator_ts_expectations: election.Date (TEXT) -> String fuzzer: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings of length ~[min,max] plus contamination; will NOT produce 'July 1942' or year formats — implausible dates drive FN on date predicates.
representative.Lifespan (TEXT) -> String fuzzer: random strings, never en-dash ranges — implausible for lifespan queries.
Name/State/Party -> String fuzzer: random strings; Party will not be 'Republican'/'Democratic' unless literal pool seeds it — FN on party filters.

Number fuzzer on INT/REAL columns: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] (scale from type args, default 0 for bare INT/REAL) then +-1/+-2 perturbation; Vote_Percent/Seats/Place get wild values, not 0-100 or small ints — FN on range predicates.
Number list-range quirk (list_max overwritten to full max) means even with literal pool the fresh draws dominate — implausible magnitudes.
PK Election_ID/Representative_ID: single-column PK -> max_l0=inf, so fresh draws never reuse; PK uniqueness enforced by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
FK election.Representative_ID draws from representative's FINAL filtered PK values with replacement — ties/duplicates in child FK expected (5 rows over 7 parents).
Tiny tables: choose_table_sizes gives 1+30*u (level 0) and x4 per level, capped 2500 — instances will be tens-to-hundreds of rows, far larger than originals; joins produce many-to-many blowups.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python; rows violating PK/unique fail at insert and are skipped — some tables may end up smaller than requested.
String contamination (suffix/prefix/drop-char) creates near-miss values that break equality joins — FP source on string joins.
Missing ties: original has Vote_Percent/Seats/Place duplicates but TS fresh draws rarely reproduce exact ties — FP on GROUP BY/HAVING tie queries.
